leading_mechanism.description: During current R5 verify-lift, the Nut starts lagging behind the EE while bilateral handle contact and approximately 26.5 N closing feedback remain. The load-bearing contact patches then migrate toward the upper handle edge, bilateral normal support declines, finger vertical force becomes downward, and only afterward does closing-force feedback collapse and contact disappear.
candidate_boundaries: shared NutAssembly grasp pose / acquisition-state generation
canonical arm trajectory / verify-lift command history
leading_mechanism.owner_note: The evidence localizes the physical event sequence but does not isolate a unique implementation owner because historical and current controller, planner, gripper-rate semantics, and authorization state differ.

frequency_findings.interpretation: 50/100/500 Hz changes event timestamps by at most 16 ms and do not materially change failure magnitude; 100 Hz is not the dominant cause under the tested shared R5 profile.

inner_servo_counterfactual.interpretation: Changing only R5 gripper update cadence to 100 Hz does not rescue retention or materially alter the failure sequence. This is not a full replay of the historical R1 gripper law/rates.

event_order.interpretation: Relative velocity and drift precede force-feedback collapse.

supported_alternatives.hypothesis: current R5 lift trajectory causes a load/patch migration that the historical grasp command history tolerates
different Nut-in-EE acquisition pose shifts contact toward an unstable handle edge
faster R5 closing and force-adjust histories create a different dynamic grasp state
100 Hz outer control alone is the cause
500 Hz gripper update alone is the cause

next_experiment.decision_rule: Attribute causality only if switching one target history on the same restored physical state changes contact-patch migration and retention reproducibly. If exact state restore is unavailable, label the crossover approximate and match the full authorization pose/finger state before interpreting it.
